To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dentition and dermis are two independent secondary developmental regions, the dentition develops early and scales late, the dentition and scales are formed by different types of cells, and that both the dentition and the scales are erupted by fluid pressures.
The dermal skeleton and the dentition of sharks develop from two independent secondary developmental regions.

the development of the dentation starts very early, the scales erupt shortly before the hatching, and the forces which erupt the teeth and scales may come from the fluid pressures in vacoules of the fibrous dermis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the dermal skeleton and dentition of the embryonic shark Scyliorhinius canicula (L.).
the development of the dentine of the teeth and of the dermal skeleton in Scyliorhynus canicula, a small shark.
the developmental biology of the dentition and dermis of Scyli orhinus caniculus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the development of dentition and scales are independent of each other, and that both are derived from two independent secondary developmental regions.
the development of the dentation and dermal skeleton are independent developmental fields, which are not only separated in space, but also in their development.

teeth are formed by ectoderm-derived odontoblast cells which produce the crown and upper part (enamel and dentine) of the base, whereas scales are formed by ectomesenchymal osteoblasts which produce the basal plate and lower part (sclerotic bone) of the base.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dentition and dermis of sharks are two distinct secondary developmental fields.
the development of the dentation and dermal skeleton of Scyliobrlnus is similar to that of the teeth and dermal skeleton, respectively, of the teleosts.
the dermal skeleton of sharks and the dentition of vertebrates are homologous structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dermal skeleton is a secondary developmental field that is independent of the dentition, and it develops in a way that is different from the dentition in terms of timing and structure.
the dentition and dermis are two independent developmental fields.
dentition and scales are formed by different developmental fields, which have different developmental and structural characteristics.
